chapters.title: The Desk, Not the Mind
chapters.tease: The model answers only from what is on its desk. If it is not on the desk, it does not exist.

chapters.title: Stateless by Design
chapters.tease: Models keep nothing between calls. Anything that looks like memory is apparatus built around them.

chapters.title: Tokens, the Unit of Everything
chapters.tease: Models read tokens, not words. Every limit, bill and measure of fit is counted in them.

chapters.title: The Window Has Edges
chapters.tease: The advertised window is a ceiling. The useful window is smaller, and you find it by testing.

chapters.title: A Conversation Is a Document
chapters.tease: A chat is a document, re-read in full from the top every time the model replies.

chapters.title: Input and Output Share the Room
chapters.tease: The prompt and the reply share one window. Fill it with input and the answer gets cut off.

chapters.title: Garbage In, Still
chapters.tease: Rubbish in a context window still comes out as rubbish, just fluent and well dressed.

chapters.title: The Prompt Was Never Enough
chapters.tease: The prompt is one paragraph on the desk. Context engineering decides everything else the model sees.

chapters.title: Context Is a Verb
chapters.tease: Context is not a fixed bundle. Every call, something decides what goes in, by design or by default.

chapters.title: The First Discipline
chapters.tease: The first discipline is subtraction: put in what the task needs, and take out everything else.

chapters.title: Tokens Are Cheap, Attention Is Not
chapters.tease: Fitting in the window is admission; being attended to is what decides the answer.

chapters.title: Attention Without the Maths
chapters.tease: The model reads everything, but for each new token it weighs some pieces far more than others.

chapters.title: Lost in the Middle
chapters.tease: Information at the start or end of a long input gets used well; in the middle, it fades.

chapters.title: Beginnings and Endings
chapters.tease: Frame at the front, sources in the middle, and the specific ask last, where it shapes the reply.

chapters.title: Similar Is Not Relevant
chapters.tease: The dangerous text is not noise; it is the near miss that answers a slightly different question.

chapters.title: The Needle Is Not the Job
chapters.tease: Finding one hidden sentence is a party trick; real work means combining facts and noticing gaps.

chapters.title: Structure Is a Kindness
chapters.tease: Headings, labels and tags are signposts the model reads; a wall of text makes it guess.

chapters.title: Saying It Twice
chapters.tease: Repeat the one rule that matters, calmly, near the end; shouting every rule makes emphasis meaningless.

chapters.title: Long Context, Short Understanding
chapters.tease: A model that has read everything knows of it, not about it; ask for inspectable work, not verdicts.

chapters.title: Read It Like the Model Does
chapters.tease: When the answer is wrong, the evidence is in the context the model actually received. Go and read it.

chapters.title: The System Prompt Is the Room
chapters.tease: The system prompt sets up the room: only what is true for every request belongs in it.

chapters.title: Write for a Clever Stranger
chapters.tease: Brief the model like a clever stranger: assume intelligence, never assume knowledge.

chapters.title: Rules Need Reasons
chapters.tease: A bare rule is applied literally; add its reason and the model generalises and bends sensibly.

chapters.title: Examples Outrank Adjectives
chapters.tease: One good example says more than a paragraph of adjectives, and two or three varied ones say it best.

chapters.title: The Trouble With Never
chapters.tease: Recast most 'never' rules as positive targets; keep only real boundaries, with their reasons.

chapters.title: The Instructions File
chapters.tease: An instructions file turns corrections you keep repeating into permanent context every session reads.

chapters.title: Layers and Precedence
chapters.tease: Standing instructions arrive in layers but the model reads one document, so give each layer one job.

chapters.title: Short Files Get Read
chapters.tease: Instruction files grow by accretion until nobody reads them; prune them so they stay heeded.

chapters.title: When Orders Contradict
chapters.tease: Contradictory instructions make the model look unreliable; find the clashes and settle each one.

chapters.title: Instructions Are Code
chapters.tease: Prompts change what your product does, so give them version control, review and tests like code.

chapters.title: Memory Is a Rented Room
chapters.tease: Models do not remember. A store outside the window is searched, and notes are handed in on each call.

chapters.title: The Two Memories
chapters.tease: Working memory is the desk, long-term memory the filing cabinet. Most trouble comes from confusing the two.

chapters.title: What Deserves Remembering
chapters.tease: Store only what is durable and changes behaviour. Remember conclusions, not conversations.

chapters.title: Writing a Good Memory
chapters.tease: A memory is a note to a stranger. Make it specific, scoped, dated and able to stand on its own.

chapters.title: The Consolidation Problem
chapters.tease: Memory stores grow by accretion into piles. Merge related entries into one current statement.

chapters.title: The Contradiction Ledger
chapters.tease: When memories clash, the world changed. Record both with dates, then supersede or ask. Never pick quietly.

chapters.title: Whose Memory Is It
chapters.tease: Memory about a person should be visible to that person, scoped by project and enforced by the system.

chapters.title: Forgetting on Purpose
chapters.tease: Every memory needs a lifetime. A system that cannot forget will remember the wrong things most of all.

chapters.title: Recall Is Not Understanding
chapters.tease: Recalling a memory is not knowing when it applies. Scope it, frame it as background, make it optional.

chapters.title: The Working Set
chapters.tease: A short progress file on disk lets long tasks survive compaction. It sits between window and long-term store.

chapters.title: Retrieval in One Breath
chapters.tease: Fetch the right text from a store you control and put it in the window before the model answers.

chapters.title: The Librarian and the Hoarder
chapters.tease: More passages is not safer: bring the few that answer, and measure where quality plateaus.

chapters.title: Chunk Wisely or Not at All
chapters.tease: Chunking is retrieval's first editorial decision: each chunk must make sense to a reader with nothing else.

chapters.title: Embeddings Find Neighbours
chapters.tease: Embeddings find passages near in meaning, but nearness is a hint about relevance, not a verdict.

chapters.title: Two Searches Are Better
chapters.tease: Keyword and semantic search fail in opposite ways: filter for eligibility, then run both and merge.

chapters.title: Rerank What You Retrieved
chapters.tease: Retrieve fifty fast, then let a reranker read question and passage together, and pass on only the best five.

chapters.title: Provenance or It Didn't Happen
chapters.tease: Every claim in a retrieved answer should trace to a labelled, dated source, or it is only an opinion.

chapters.title: The Freshness Tax
chapters.tease: An index is only as current as its last update, and stale passages arrive with full confidence.

chapters.title: When Retrieval Should Refuse
chapters.tease: When nothing relevant is found, the system should say so instead of answering from weak passages.

chapters.title: Let the Model Go Looking
chapters.tease: Give the model search tools and let it search, read and refine until it has direct evidence.

chapters.title: Tool Results Are Context
chapters.tease: Tool output is context, usually most of it, and almost nobody designs it to be read.

chapters.title: The Description Is a Prompt
chapters.tease: Tool names and descriptions are instructions the model reads every turn. Vague in, vague use out.

chapters.title: Trim Before You Return
chapters.tease: Return less. Trim tool output to what the next step needs, and let the model ask for the rest.

chapters.title: Errors That Teach
chapters.tease: An error message is an instruction. Say what went wrong and how to fix it, and the model retries right.

chapters.title: Pages, Not Floods
chapters.tease: Never return everything by default. Page large results, give a total, and say how to get more.

chapters.title: Pointers, Not Payloads
chapters.tease: Pass references, not content. Give the model an index and let it open what each step needs.

chapters.title: Data, Not Instructions
chapters.tease: Everything a tool brings in from outside is something to read, not someone to obey.

chapters.title: Too Many Tools
chapters.tease: Past a point, more tools mean worse choices. Curate, group and defer so the agent stays sharp.

chapters.title: The File System as Memory
chapters.tease: The window is for thinking, the disk is for keeping. Save large outputs and notes to files.

chapters.title: Design the Return Trip
chapters.tease: Design tools around the context they produce: write the return first, then build the tool.

chapters.title: Sessions Grow Heavy
chapters.tease: Long sessions get heavier every turn, and quality fades quietly long before the window is full.

chapters.title: Compaction
chapters.tease: Compaction swaps a long history for a summary, and the summary decides what the next hour remembers.

chapters.title: What a Good Summary Keeps
chapters.tease: A summary for continuing work answers five questions: what, where, why, what is broken, what is next.

chapters.title: Clear and Begin Again
chapters.tease: When the task changes or the session goes in circles, write a brief, clear the window and begin again.

chapters.title: The Handover Note
chapters.tease: Agents start every session with no memory, so write a handover note before each session ends.

chapters.title: Prompt Caching
chapters.tease: Providers can reuse the processing of a repeated prefix, so a stable start makes calls cheaper and faster.

chapters.title: Stable First, Volatile Last
chapters.tease: Attention, caching and maintenance all agree: put stable material first and volatile material last.

chapters.title: The Long Document
chapters.tease: Read a long document whole when you need its shape, and in parts when each part needs the same job.

chapters.title: Quote, Then Answer
chapters.tease: Ask the model to quote the relevant passages exactly, then answer from those quotes alone.

chapters.title: Map, Then Reduce
chapters.tease: When material will not fit one window, process each piece separately, then combine the results.

chapters.title: Isolation Is the Point
chapters.tease: A subagent's real value is isolation: it reads everything so the parent's window does not have to.

chapters.title: Briefing a Subagent
chapters.tease: A subagent knows only what the brief says, so write the brief as if that were true, because it is.

chapters.title: What Comes Back
chapters.tease: A subagent's report is context for the parent: the answer, the evidence and the doubts, not the journey.

chapters.title: The Delegation Trap
chapters.tease: Splitting coupled work across agents loses the thread: divide the reading freely, the deciding with care.

chapters.title: Parallel Windows
chapters.tease: Independent tasks fly in parallel windows, but they multiply the tokens, not the judgement that ties them.

chapters.title: Shared State Lives Outside
chapters.tease: Windows cannot see each other, so shared knowledge lives outside them: in files, task lists and the repo.

chapters.title: The Repo Will Not Fit
chapters.tease: No window holds a real codebase, so load what the task touches, not what exists, like any good developer.

chapters.title: Map Before Territory
chapters.tease: Build a map first, structure then search, so every read that follows lands on the right code.

chapters.title: Tests Are Context
chapters.tease: Fast, clear tests give an agent feedback after every change, so it iterates to correct, not just plausible.

chapters.title: The Plan Is a File
chapters.tease: Put the plan in a file, not the conversation: it survives compaction, guides subagents and is easy to steer.

chapters.title: Budget the Window
chapters.tease: A context window is a budget: decide where the tokens go, or they will decide for you.

chapters.title: Tokens Times Turns
chapters.tease: In a loop, every token you keep is re-read on every later step, so cost is tokens times turns.

chapters.title: Audit What Is In There
chapters.tease: Audit real contexts regularly: what is actually in the window, not what the design says should be.

chapters.title: Context Rot
chapters.tease: Quality slips as the context grows, well before the window is full: crowded is enough to fail.

chapters.title: Context Poisoning
chapters.tease: One error in the context becomes a premise every later step builds on; remove it, do not just correct it.

chapters.title: Context Distraction
chapters.tease: Accurate but unneeded material pulls the model off-task; the fix is usually to take something away.

chapters.title: Context Clash
chapters.tease: When sources contradict, hidden clashes become a coin toss; labelled ones become a flagged answer.

chapters.title: The Echo of Its Own Mistakes
chapters.tease: Every reply becomes an example the model imitates, so breaking a rut means changing the context.

chapters.title: Test the Context, Not the Model
chapters.tease: Most model problems are context problems: test retrieval, ranking and placement before the model.

chapters.title: A Post-Mortem for Prompts
chapters.tease: Every bad answer was a reasonable reading of some context; rebuild it and find the cause.

chapters.title: Bigger Windows Will Not Save You
chapters.tease: Bigger windows move the edge rather than remove it, so choosing what goes in stays the discipline.

chapters.title: The Context Becomes the Product
chapters.tease: Models are a shared commodity; your advantage is the context you assemble around them.

chapters.title: Agents Talking to Agents
chapters.tease: When agents brief agents, every handoff is a context boundary, so design briefs and returns deliberately.

chapters.title: Portable Habits
chapters.tease: Habits grounded in the problem survive model changes; model-specific tricks are calibration to re-measure.

chapters.title: Your Own Context Window
chapters.tease: You have a context window too: curate your own attention with the care you give a model's.

chapters.title: Curation Is Self-Respect
chapters.tease: Curation is not a chore before the work; it is respect for the model, the people downstream and yourself.

chapters.title: Delegate the Task, Keep the Judgement
chapters.tease: Delegate reading and drafting, keep the judgement about context: responsibility does not delegate.

chapters.title: A Daily Practice
chapters.tease: Choose the context, watch the window, keep the notes, check the work: small habits beat clever prompts.

chapters.title: The Context Is Yours
chapters.tease: The model reads the page you prepare, so results trace back to your choices and are yours to fix.

chapters.title: What You Leave Out
chapters.tease: What you leave out of the context window is the real prompt; every inclusion should be a choice.
